name: pediatric orthopedics overview
title: Pediatric orthopedics: an injury (fracture pattern, growth plate, apophysis) or a developmental problem (hip dysplasia, clubfoot, leg shape, scoliosis); each column gives presentation, exam and x-ray, and treatment

root.title: A child's bone or joint problem: an INJURY, or a DEVELOPMENTAL problem?
lines: children's bone is porous and pliable, the periosteum thick, and the growth plate (physis) the weak point: a child FRACTURES where an adult sprains

groups.title: INJURY
lines: falls from low heights · sport · pedestrian struck · infant or toddler: NON-ACCIDENTAL injury

groups.title: DEVELOPMENTAL
lines: screen, then treat early; do not overtreat normal variants

head: h
Fractures of pliable bone
buckle · greenstick · plastic deformation · avulsion
healing seldom a problem: 'ends in the same room'
pres: less ligament injury or dislocation than adults
tx: hematoma block or conscious sedation (most control)
casting is ACTIVE treatment: alignment criteria by age
reductions fail: not pre-planned, force direction ignored (translation AND angulation), poor moulding, excess padding, cast too short

head: h
Growth plate: Salter-Harris
risk: growth ARREST → leg length or angular deformity
pres: sprains are rare in kids: think Salter-Harris I
~ ~10% develop a growth disturbance: age, severity, type IV-V, reduction method, plate blood supply, open injury
inv: • IV: metaphysis-epiphysis bony bridge risk · lateral humeral condyle, distal tibia
often missed; found late as growth arrest · refer to orthopedics
arrest: angulation, length difference · treat by growth left
tx: EVERY growth plate injury is serious

head: h
Apophysis
tendon insertion: pulled by fast growth + tight muscle
pres: case: 14 M, 100 m dash → acute hip pain, antalgic limp
• Osgood-Schlatter: tibial tuberosity microavulsions, tender, swollen, gradual
other adolescent overuse: stress fracture · osteochondritis dissecans (bone under cartilage loses blood, may come loose)
tx: • apophysitis: rest, ice, compression, elevation; activity as tolerated; anti-inflammatories as needed

head: h
Developmental dysplasia of the hip
shallow acetabulum → subluxation or dislocation
1-6 per 1000 live births · LEFT > right
pres: • Caucasian, North American Indigenous (less: Black, Asian)
inv: • Barlow, sign of EXIT: hip slips OUT (adduct, push back) · reduce it
• Ortolani, sign of ENTRY: hip slips back IN (abduct, lift on the greater trochanter)

head: h
Clubfoot
congenital talipes equinovarus
ankle plantarflexed · heel and forefoot in varus
inv: progressive deformity and stiffness; walking and footwear suffer
tx: full time 3 months, then nights 2-3 years
posteromedial release: lengthen contracted structures, realign

head: h
Leg shape
in-toeing · out-toeing · bow legs · knock knees
inv: • nutritional deficiency, metabolic bone disease, skeletal dysplasia, old trauma
tx: in-toeing, out-toeing: very common referral, normal variation · flat feet

head: h
Scoliosis
lateral curve + rotation · idiopathic: adolescent, F > M
neuromuscular (cerebral palsy, spina bifida, neurofibromatosis) · congenital · post-traumatic
pres: • neuro review of systems · family, past history
inv: • rib prominence on the convex side
• full neuro exam · skin: dimple, hairy patch, lipoma, hemangioma
e.g. right thoracic T7-T12, 45° · rule out congenital, trauma, tumour
tx: to STOP progression · by curve size and risk

panels.title: Pediatric elbow
items: ossification centres appear in order CRITOE at about 1 · 3 · 5 · 7 · 9 · 11 years: capitellum, radial head, internal (medial) epicondyle, trochlea, olecranon, external (lateral) epicondyle

young: little or no ossification, limited exam · swelling = suspect a bony injury, especially unossified · call pediatric orthopedics for a very swollen elbow, instability, a displaced fracture or an incongruously reduced dislocation

panels.title: A limping child
items: causes differ by AGE: missed hip dysplasia · clubfoot · hip disease (transient synovitis, Perthes, slipped capital femoral epiphysis) · overuse · trauma, accidental or not · neuromuscular, inflammatory arthritis
warning signs in any abnormal gait: asymmetry · progressive · leg length difference · pain · deformity
see the CHILD WITH A LIMP chart
